extraction.name: BoolQ
extraction.description: A reading comprehension dataset of 16,000 naturally occurring yes/no questions. Each question is paired with a Wikipedia paragraph marked by an annotator as containing the answer, and the task is to return "yes" or "no".
extraction.creator: Christopher Clark, Kenton Lee, Ming-Wei Chang, Tom Kwiatkowski, Michael Collins, Kristina Toutanova
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by gathering a large number of additional natural yes/no questions, building on Natural Questions, with each example consisting of a question, a paragraph from a Wikipedia article, the article title, and a yes/no answer.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Natural yes/no questions paired with paragraphs and titles from Wikipedia articles, plus yes/no answers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd-sourced entailment/yes-no examples were used, but the section does not describe the specific labeling task instructions, annotator workforce, or quality control process.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset appears to contain answer-correlated artifacts in passages, with some passage language patterns correlating with yes/no labels.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset/task remains challenging with a substantial gap to human performance, and some transfer approaches were ineffective.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a dedicated yes/no question answering reading comprehension benchmark, with train/dev usage for model training and evaluation; the paper also uses it for transfer learning experiments.

name.evidence: We build a reading comprehension dataset, BoolQ, of such questions

description.evidence: We follow the data collection method used by Natural Questions (NQ) (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019) to gather 16,000 naturally occurring yes/no questions into a dataset we call BoolQ (for Boolean Questions). Each question is paired with a paragraph from Wikipedia that an independent annotator has marked as containing the answer. The task is then to take a question and passage as input, and to return “yes” or “no” as output.
